status: OPEN — CRITICAL, UNRESOLVED — see CLAUDE.md's critical-flag entry for the same date
severity: CRITICAL — permanent, silent, single-client cross-replica divergence, reachable via ORDINARY LIVE EDITING (no reconnection, no offline queueing, no fault injection of any kind)
oneLineDescription: A continuously-connected client's ordinary localInsert() can anchor (via FugueTree.decidePlacement's leftmostDescendant branch) to a tombstoned node that the server has since physically garbage-collected (Engine.collect()) once the stability frontier and undo-horizon conditions are met — the operation then buffers in the server's engine.pending PERMANENTLY, and the client's own local engine has already integrated the content with no mechanism to revert it, producing a silent, permanent divergence between that one client and every other replica.
discoveredDuring: Phase 25 M8-e soak test DoD verification (packages/server/src/db/soak.db.test.ts) — the soak run's own final assertion failed (coordinator.engine.pending.length === 1400, expected 0). Investigating that failure surfaced this general mechanism, which the user explicitly asked to be checked against a REAL, continuously-connected SyncClient (not just the soak test's own simplified simulated-client harness) before accepting the soak failure as a mere test-fixture gap. The check confirmed the race is real and general, not specific to the soak harness.

mechanism.step1: Client and server converge on 'AB' via two ordinary inserts (opA: parent=null,side=R; opB: parent=opA.id,side=R, a chain — opB is opA's own right child).
mechanism.step2: The client deletes 'B' (delB, target=opB.id) — an entirely ordinary user action. Applied to both client and server; the server records real GC delete-context (seq/atMs), exactly as writePath.ts does for every real delete.
mechanism.step3: The server's Engine.collect() physically removes opB. Its condition 3 ('no live node currently anchors this') is evaluated purely against the SERVER's OWN current tree — it has no way to know about operations the client has not yet minted or sent. RFC's own undo-horizon grace period (default 5 minutes / 200 ops per replica, explicitly flagged in the RFC as 'unvalidated') is a heuristic DELAY, not a structural proof of safety — it does not prevent this, it only makes it less likely to happen within the grace window.
mechanism.step4: The CLIENT is never told opB was collected — Engine Spec's own design has GC broadcast nothing to clients, and no client ever runs its own GC. opB remains fully present (tombstoned) in the client's own local Fugue tree forever, completely independent of what the server does with its own copy.
mechanism.step5: The client later performs an ORDINARY new local insert (opD) at the end of 'A' — nothing about this is reconnection, reconciliation, or offline queueing; it is exactly what a live, continuously-connected user's next keystroke looks like. FugueTree.decidePlacement(visibleIndex=1)'s SECOND branch fires (leftOriginNode=opA already has a right child, opB) and calls leftmostDescendant(opB) — which performs NO deleted-status check at all — returning opB itself as the new operation's parent, even though opB is tombstoned.
mechanism.step6: The client's own engine applies opD SYNCHRONOUSLY at mint time (fundamental to this project's real-time-feel design since Phase 3/10) — the client's own view becomes 'AD' immediately and permanently, with no network round trip required to see it.
mechanism.step7: opD is sent to the server. Engine.applyRemote(opD) finds opB no longer exists (ready() fails) — opD buffers into server.engine.pending. Because opB can never come back, this buffering is PERMANENT, not a transient reordering that resolves in milliseconds (the normal case writePath.ts's own comments describe).
mechanism.consequence: The client's own document permanently shows 'AD'; the server (and therefore every other real peer) permanently shows only 'A'. Nothing in the currently-shipped system reverts the client's own already-integrated insert — Engine has no 'undo one specific already-integrated operation' primitive (Undelete's structural inverse, Phase 36, does not apply here and remains unbuilt anyway). offlineWindowScheduler.ts's Rule 7.2 sweep will eventually (default 30s) explicitly reject opD server-side rather than leave it stuck in engine.pending forever, and SyncClient's Phase 24 preserve-rule machinery will retain its CONTENT in rejectedOps rather than silently lose it — but neither mechanism removes the character from the authoring client's own visible document. The result is a silent, permanent, single-character (or more, for anything typed after it) divergence that the affected user has no way to discover from the product's own UI.

minimalReproduction.description: Fully deterministic, no real time or network required — mirrors verified engine.ts semantics directly. Verified passing as packages/engine/src/regressionR0012.test.ts (permanent, in the default pnpm test suite).
minimalReproduction.engineConstruction: Two Engine instances (replicaId 1 = 'client', replicaId 0 = 'server'), built to identical converged state via applyRemote, exactly as a real client/server pair would be after ordinary sync.

operationStream.note: opB (id {c:2,r:1}) is now PHYSICALLY REMOVED from the server's tree — server.hasIdentifier({c:2,r:1}) === false

operationStream.step: client.localInsert(1, 'D')  -- an ORDINARY new keystroke, not reconciliation
operationStream.note: parent === opB.id — the client anchored to the node the server already collected, purely via FugueTree.decidePlacement's own leftmostDescendant branch
client's own view: succeeded immediately and permanently
PERMANENT — opB will never exist again, so this never resolves on its own
server (and every other real peer) never sees 'D' — this is the silent, permanent divergence

whyThisIsDifferentFromR0008ThroughR0011: R0008-R0011 were defects in the CRDT placement/ordering algorithm itself (YATA-family, since replaced by Fugue). This is not a placement-algorithm defect — Fugue's decidePlacement and collect() are each individually CORRECT per their own specifications. This is a defect in the INTERACTION between three independently-correct components: (1) GC's condition 3 can only ever see the server's own current tree, structurally blind to future client operations by construction; (2) the undo horizon is an explicitly-unvalidated heuristic delay, not a structural safety proof; (3) the client has no mechanism to learn that a node it still holds locally has been server-side collected, and no mechanism to revert an already-integrated local operation if that node turns out to have been needed. Fixing this requires a cross-component design decision (see CLAUDE.md's critical-flag entry for the options under consideration), not a single-function algorithm patch.
whyThisIsNOTPreventedByPhase24sExistingS: Phase 24's own reconcileOfflineQueue.ts proof (see CLAUDE.md's Key Technical Decisions entry on this) is SCOPED SPECIFICALLY to the reconnection-reconciliation code path (visibleIndexAfter/visibleIndexOfTarget), which always re-resolves an anchor against CURRENT structure at reconciliation time and therefore can never name a stale identifier. Ordinary Engine.localInsert() — the function every live keystroke calls — does not go through that path at all; it uses FugueTree.decidePlacement directly against whatever node objects already exist in the resident tree, with no re-resolution step of any kind. offlineWindowScheduler.ts's Rule 7.2 sweep (also Phase 24) DOES correctly prevent the server-side PERMANENT-BUFFERING half of this from being silent forever (it explicit-rejects after 30s by default) — but it does nothing about the CLIENT-side half: the affected user's own document has already, synchronously, silently diverged, and nothing currently reverts it.
reproducibilityCaveat: None — this fully satisfies Test Plan §2.3 Rule 3 (a complete, byte-exact, deterministic operation stream), unlike R0001-R0007. No fault injection, timing, network, or randomness of any kind is required to reproduce it.
